X-15 Authorization layers 2–3: staff roles

Bangla name: অথরাইজেশন স্তর ২–৩: স্টাফ রোল

← 60 · Cross-cutting · Contents · Open queries

1. Name and purpose

Staff roles. Admin-pool users carry their roles in the Cognito attribute custom:role (comma-separated). The Admin and UserIssue services turn that attribute into role claims on each request (layer 2) and controllers allow or deny by role with [Authorize(Roles = …)] (layer 3). This file explains the mechanism and gives the role × controller matrix of the Admin service.

2. Trigger and actor

Every request with an Admin-pool token to the Admin or UserIssue service.

Role value Code constant Meaning (from menus and controllers)
admin Role.Admin Full administrator
event_manager Role.EventManager Programs, venues, events, notices, raffle, gate assignment
ticket_manager Role.TicketManager Events, ticket layouts/attributes, ticket checkers, reserved-ticket generation
ticket_operator Role.BCBPersonnel BCB personnel: dashboard, events, reports, reserved-ticket generation
customer_support Role.CustomerSupportAdmin Customer issues

3. Business flow

An administrator gives a staff member one or more roles (and programs) in the admin portal (X-05). From then on the staff member sees the matching menu (X-17) and the backend allows only the matching endpoints.

4. Technical flow

# Step Detail
1 Authenticate Default scheme admin validates the token (X-14)
2 Enrich CognitoUserAttributesMiddleware (registered in Admin and UserIssue only): reads sub; picks the pool from the scope claim (aws.cognito.signin.user.admin → Admin pool); calls Cognito AdminGetUser(pool, sub) through the cache User, key user_{sub}; adds one ClaimTypes.Role claim per comma-separated value of custom:role, and one program_id claim per value of custom:program_ids
3 Authorize [Authorize(Roles = "a,b")] passes if the user has any listed role. Class and method attributes both apply (logical AND)
4 Failure Missing role → 403. Enrichment errors are logged and swallowed, so the request continues without roles and ends in 403

Cache: ICacheManager is a distributed (Redis) cache with a default absolute expiry of 2 minutes for every cache (Core/ETP.Core/Configuration/CacheConfig.cs:13, :40-43). The Admin service removes user_{id} when it updates or deletes a staff user (X-05).

✔* Checker tokens on ticket-checker-gate: the class attribute accepts the TicketChecker scheme and role ticket-checker, so a checker's token can call every method of this controller that has no stricter method attribute, including force-assign, force-unassign, update-download-status, remove-user, report, export, duplicate-tickets and manual-entry-tickets.

Outside the Admin service roles are not checked: Booking, Ticketing and UserIssue use Policy = admin, which accepts any Admin-pool user (X-14).

6. API contracts

Not an endpoint. The role claims are visible only on the server.

7. Data and side effects

One Cognito AdminGetUser call per user every 2 minutes per cache miss.

9. Handover notes

  1. Pool selection by scope works by accident. aws.cognito.signin.user.admin is the standard scope of every Cognito access token from SDK sign-in, so the middleware always looks in the Admin pool. That is correct only because the default scheme is admin: tokens from other pools are never authenticated by the default scheme, so the middleware never sees them (architecture §2.5, observation 2).
  2. Role changes take effect within 2 minutes (cache), immediately on the Admin instance that made the change, and only after the portal refreshes its own 55-minute cache (X-17).
  3. ticket_manager cannot manage gates (ticket-checker-gate omits it), although the menu groups gates with events.
  4. Checker tokens are accepted on admin gate operations (✔* above). Review whether that is intended.
  5. Middleware order in Admin: UseAuthentication → UseAuthorization → ProgramIdMiddleware → CognitoUserAttributesMiddleware → … → UseRouting → UseAuthentication → UseAuthorization. Endpoint authorization runs in the second pair, after the claims were added. Keep that order if you touch Program.cs.
